findings.title: Stale-session rejection raises AttributeError for duck-typed user models (CWE-755)
findings.why_it_matters: For a user model that implements its own get_session_auth_hash() without inheriting AbstractBaseUser (a setup docs/topics/auth/default.txt:920-923 explicitly supports), every request carrying a session whose hash no longer matches -- i.e. exactly the 'other sessions after a password change' case -- now fails with AttributeError instead of being flushed and treated as anonymous. The stale session is never flushed, so it keeps erroring on each request (500 from login_required and similar) until the cookie is cleared, and the documented log-out-on-password-change behaviour degrades to a persistent error. The branch is entered under a hasattr(user, "get_session_auth_hash") guard only, but then unconditionally calls the new get_session_auth_fallback_hash(); guarding the fallback call the same way restores the previous flush-and-anonymous outcome for models without the new method.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the fallback lookup with the same duck-typing convention used for get_session_auth_hash, so objects lacking the new method fall through to flush: `if session_hash and hasattr(user, "get_session_auth_fallback_hash") and any(constant_time_compare(session_hash, h) for h in user.get_session_auth_fallback_hash()):` ... else flush() and user = None. Add a test with a user object exposing only get_session_auth_hash and a mismatching session hash, asserting AnonymousUser is returned and the session is flushed. Assumption: non-AbstractBaseUser models remain supported, per docs/topics/auth/default.txt:920-923.
evidence: django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:215 -- `for fallback_auth_hash in user.get_session_auth_fallback_hash()` (called unconditionally inside the mismatch branch)
django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:200 -- `if hasattr(user, "get_session_auth_hash"):` (the only capability check guarding the block; nothing checks for get_session_auth_fallback_hash)
django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:141 -- `def get_session_auth_fallback_hash(self):` is defined only on AbstractBaseUser; grep finds no other definition in django/

docs/topics/auth/default.txt:920-923 -- 'If your AUTH_USER_MODEL inherits from AbstractBaseUser or implements its own get_session_auth_hash() method, authenticated sessions will include the hash returned by this function.'
django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:220-221 -- `request.session.flush()` / `user = None` are in the else arm and are never reached once line 215 raises

django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:35 -- `request.user = SimpleLazyObject(lambda: get_user(request))`: the exception surfaces on first request.user attribute access; access is denied (fail-closed) but the session is not invalidated

residual_risks: Fallback hashes are computed by the private AbstractBaseUser._get_session_auth_hash(secret=...) (base_user.py:141-152), bypassing any subclass override of get_session_auth_hash(). Normally this fails closed (overriding models still lose sessions on key rotation unless they also override get_session_auth_fallback_hash), but a session still holding a default password-HMAC under a fallback key is accepted and re-stamped (auth/__init__.py:213-218) even if the project later introduced an override intended to invalidate existing sessions. Not confirmed as exploitable; depends on project-specific overrides.

By design, any key left in SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS now also validates the session auth hash, so the session-auth-hash check no longer requires the current SECRET_KEY. With the signed_cookies session backend (cookie signature already accepts fallbacks, core/signing.py:115) a holder of a retired key plus a user's stored password hash can construct an accepted authenticated session until that key is removed. This matches the documented rotation semantics (docs/howto/deployment/checklist.txt:72 'removed ... in a timely manner') and is not a defect in the diff.
testing_gaps: No test asserts the negative path with fallbacks configured: a session whose hash matches neither SECRET_KEY nor any SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS entry must be flushed and yield AnonymousUser (the only added test, tests/auth_tests/test_basic.py:144, covers the positive path).
No test asserts that a password change still invalidates a session whose stored hash was derived from a fallback key (the intent's 'must not weaken session invalidation on password change').
